shipped_row.boundary_rationale: The psalm opens with the verse-initial hodu-le-YHWH call: “Give thanks to Yahweh!” (web:Ps.105.1), with the Hebrew 'הוֹד֣וּ לַ֭יהוָה' at oshb:Ps.105.1, a tier-1 opener device (psalm_device_inventory.json hodu_openings). The imperative cluster continues: “Call on his name” (web:Ps.105.1), “Sing to him, sing praises to him” (web:Ps.105.2), “Glory in his holy name” (web:Ps.105.3), “Seek Yahweh and his strength” (web:Ps.105.4), and also “Remember his marvelous works” (web:Ps.105.5), before the unit closes addressing “you offspring of Abraham… you children of Jacob, his chosen ones” (web:Ps.105.6), naming the addressees the historical recital that follows will retell.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Closing the unit at 105:5 (its final imperative) and giving the vocative “offspring of Abraham” (web:Ps.105.6) its own row was considered, but 105:6 is the vocative addressee of 105:5’s “remember,” not its grammatical object, so splitting it would sever the imperative from its addressee.
observed_substrate_signals: verse-initial hodu-le-YHWH opener ('הוֹד֣וּ לַ֭יהוָה', 105:1, oshb:Ps.105.1), tier-1 device per the frame inventory
sustained imperative-cluster mode runs 105:1-6 (give thanks, call, sing, glory, seek, remember), closing on the vocative addressee it governs
shipped_row.device_notes: Psalm 105 coheres as one composition — parent grouping Psalm 105; every row below shares that single parent. The historical recital moves covenant → Joseph → Egypt/plagues → exodus → settlement across the rows that follow.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: The mode shifts to jussive petition: “Let Yahweh's glory endure forever” (web:Ps.104.31), the Hebrew 'יְהִ֤י כְב֣וֹד יְהוָ֣ה לְעוֹלָ֑ם' at oshb:Ps.104.31, a grammatical break from the second-person description preceding it. Third-person description of Yahweh’s power returns at 104:32, then the psalmist’s own first-person vow opens at “I will sing to Yahweh as long as I live” (web:Ps.104.33); the Hebrew 'אָשִׁ֣ירָה' underlies it at oshb:Ps.104.33, and continues through 104:34, before the unit closes with a wish against sinners, the psalm’s own inclusio — “Bless Yahweh, my soul” (web:Ps.104.35), in Hebrew 'בָּרֲכִ֣י נַ֭פְשִׁי' (oshb:Ps.104.35) — and the hallelu-Yah that ends the psalm: 'הַֽלְלוּ יָֽהּ' (oshb:Ps.104.35).
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the closing doxology (104:31-32) from the first-person vow and final wish (104:33-35) as two rows was considered, but no selah or addressee-class break separates them, and the inclusio at 104:35 answers the imperative that opened the whole psalm at 104:1, tying the closing movement together as one unit.
observed_substrate_signals: jussive mode 'יְהִ֤י' opens the doxological turn (104:31, oshb:Ps.104.31), grammatical mood shift from the preceding second-person providence cluster
first-person vow ('אָשִׁ֣ירָה', oshb:Ps.104.33) opens at 104:33, a further register shift within the same unit

inclusio 'בָּרֲכִ֣י נַ֭פְשִׁי' (oshb:Ps.104.35) closes the unit, matching the psalm's opening 'בָּרֲכִ֥י נַפְשִׁ֗י' (oshb:Ps.104.1) at accent_stripped/skeleton tier (byte tier differs: word 1 merkha at 104:1 vs munach at 104:35, word 2 revia at 104:1 vs dehi at 104:35), then hallelu-Yah closes the psalm verse-finally
prev_row.device_notes: Psalm 104 closes with 'הַֽלְלוּ יָֽהּ' (oshb:Ps.104.35), the earliest by psalm order among the curated hallelu-Yah frame inventory’s 25 book-wide occurrences (psalm_device_inventory.json: sweep: 11 verse-initial + 13 verse-final + 1 interior = 25); a naive skeleton substring sweep for 'הללו יה' returns 26 hits because it also matches the imperfect verb 'yehalelu' ('they will praise') run directly into the start of the divine name at oshb:Ps.22.27 — a consonantal false positive, not a hallelu-Yah particle; the curated inventory, not the naive sweep, is the count of record. As texture: of the two psalms following in this cluster, Ps 105 opens with the hodu-le-YHWH formula (not hallelu-Yah) and closes with hallelu-Yah only (web:Ps.105.45); only Ps 106 genuinely both opens (web:Ps.106.1) and closes (web:Ps.106.48) with the hallelu-Yah frame — texture, not evidence bearing on this row's own close.

next_row.boundary_rationale: A declarative statement opens the unit with its own independent pronoun: “He is Yahweh, our God” (web:Ps.105.7) — the Hebrew reads 'ה֭וּא יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ' (oshb:Ps.105.7) — turning from the imperative calls of 105:1-6 to covenant declaration. “He has remembered his covenant forever” (web:Ps.105.8) names “the covenant which he made with Abraham, his oath to Isaac” (web:Ps.105.9), matching 'לְיִשְׂחָֽק' at oshb:Ps.105.9, confirmed “to Jacob… to Israel” (web:Ps.105.10), and closes with the land grant quoted in direct speech: “To you I will give the land of Canaan, the lot of your inheritance” (web:Ps.105.11).
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Closing the unit at 105:10 and giving the quoted land grant (105:11) its own row was considered, but 105:11’s “saying” clause is the direct object of 105:8-10’s covenant-remembering, not a new speech act beginning a fresh unit.
observed_substrate_signals: independent-pronoun declaration 'ה֭וּא' opens the unit (105:7, oshb:Ps.105.7), a subject-class shift from the imperative mode of 105:1-6
covenant chain runs patriarch-by-patriarch (Abraham 105:9, Jacob/Israel 105:10) to its quoted land-grant close (105:11)
next_row.device_notes: The oath “to Isaac” (web:Ps.105.9) at 105:9 is spelled 'לְיִשְׂחָֽק' (oshb:Ps.105.9) with sin rather than the standard tzade; a skeleton sweep of the lamed-prefixed spelling as quoted ('לישחק') returns 1 verse book-wide (105:9 only), while a skeleton sweep of the bare-root spelling (ישחק, lamed stripped) returns 4 verses book-wide (Ps.2.4, Ps.37.13, Ps.52.6, Ps.105.9) — the other three are the common verb 'he will laugh' (root s-h-q), a consonantal homograph found elsewhere in the Psalter; a skeleton sweep for the standard tzade spelling returns 0 verses book-wide, so 105:9 is the Psalter’s one occurrence of Isaac’s name, and it carries the alternate spelling.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: A new wayyiqtol verb introduces a new named subject: “Israel also came into Egypt” (web:Ps.105.23) — MT reads 'וַיָּבֹ֣א יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל מִצְרָ֑יִם' (oshb:Ps.105.23) — turning from Joseph individually to Israel corporately. “He increased his people greatly” (web:Ps.105.24) and “turned their heart to hate his people” (web:Ps.105.25) set up the oppression that “He sent Moses, his servant, and Aaron” answers (web:Ps.105.26), the Hebrew 'שָׁ֭לַח מֹשֶׁ֣ה עַבְדּ֑וֹ' at oshb:Ps.105.26; the unit closes with Moses and Aaron performing “miracles among them, and wonders in the land of Ham” (web:Ps.105.27), the general statement the plague catalogue itemizes from 105:28.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: Untitled, Psalm 107 opens Book V with the imperative “הֹד֣וּ” (oshb:Ps.107.1), spelled defectively at byte tier -- the he takes no mater vav, against the verb's usual full spelling. Sweep of the verse-initial hodu-la-Yahweh formula (psalm_device_inventory.json hodu_openings, skeleton tier, both spellings checked) finds 6 such openings book-wide; this is the only one spelled defectively (1 of 6), the other 5 in full. The verse continues “Give thanks to Yahweh, for he is good, for his loving kindness endures forever.” (web:Ps.107.1), then the summons turns outward: “Let the redeemed by Yahweh say so, whom he has redeemed from the hand of the adversary,” (web:Ps.107.2) and “and gathered out of the lands, from the east and from the west, from the north and from the south.” (web:Ps.107.3). These three verses name no particular company and carry neither the cry-refrain nor the yodu-refrain that structures the four rescue-vignettes beginning at 107:4; they form the psalm's general frame, addressed to the redeemed of Yahweh as a class before that class is broken into its particular companies.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row through 107:4 to fold in the wilderness company was considered, but 107:4 opens the psalm's own rescue-vignette sequence with a named plight, while 1-3 names no company and carries neither refrain that binds the vignettes to follow.

I will wake up the dawn.” (web:Ps.108.2 = oshb:Ps.108.3), “I will give thanks to you, Yahweh, among the nations. I will sing praises to you among the peoples.” (web:Ps.108.3 = oshb:Ps.108.4), “For your loving kindness is great above the heavens. This unit is this psalm's earlier source-panel: its Hebrew closely parallels, without running word for word throughout, the tail of Psalm 57 -- the closing line “ר֣וּמָה עַל שָׁמַ֣יִם אֱלֹהִ֑ים וְעַ֖ל כָּל הָאָ֣רֶץ כְּבוֹדֶֽךָ” (oshb:Ps.108.6) is a close paraphrase of Psalm 57's own doxology line, not a verbatim match (oshb:Ps.57.12 collates at tier none against it; the sole divergence is the conjunctive vav on "and upon"). The genuine byte-tier anchor sits two verses earlier: “ע֭וּרָֽה הַנֵּ֥בֶל וְכִנּ֗וֹר” (web:Ps.108.2 = oshb:Ps.108.3) collates byte-identical against the tail of oshb:Ps.57.9 (“ע֭וּרָֽה הַנֵּ֥בֶל וְכִנּ֗וֹר אָעִ֥ירָה שָּֽׁחַר”), the wake-the-dawn call Psalm 57 itself doubles from a longer opening. Two verses after that shared line, the divine name differs: oshb:Ps.57.10's parallel line names Adonai where oshb:Ps.108.4 names Yahweh in the same slot -- WEB keeps that distinction, rendering Psalm 57's word "Lord" (web:Ps.57.9) against Psalm 108's "Yahweh" (“I will give thanks to you, Yahweh, among the nations. I will sing praises to you among the peoples.”, web:Ps.108.3).
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Running this row through 108:6 to keep the whole psalm's earlier half together was considered, but 108:6 (oshb:Ps.108.7) is the verse whose wording turns to match Psalm 60 rather than Psalm 57, so the panel seam sits at 108:5|108:6. A second alternative -- treating 108:1-5 as continuous with Psalm 57's own rows rather than as Psalm 108's own material -- is rejected outright: the shared wording is a typed cross-psalm relation, not a merge; Psalm 108 keeps its own single parent throughout.
